EDUC_X404.10 · 3 units

AI in Higher Education.

Engage with experts and colleagues to use AI thoughtfully in postsecondary teaching and learning, with an emphasis on scaffolding instruction and protecting essential skill development.

Notify me about the next cohort →Contact Tamara Tate

Course overview

Keep learning at the center.

This three-unit course gives higher education instructors and instructional support professionals a practical foundation in generative AI, its affordances and limitations, and the AI literacy needed for responsible use in postsecondary environments.

No prior coding or computer science experience is required. The program is designed for educators at all levels of technical experience.

FormatCollaborative, applied learning
MaterialsArticles and resources provided
TechnologyInternet-connected computer, microphone, and webcam

Course objectives

What you will be able to do.

  • Explain key AI concepts and ethical issues in clear, accessible formats.
  • Evaluate AI tools for teaching and learning, including their limitations and ethical implications.
  • Apply AI tools to teaching, learning, and administrative workflows.
  • Teach AI concepts using engaging and responsible strategies.
  • Create an AI-infused lesson tailored to your students and subject area.
  • Improve learning designs through feedback and collaboration with other educators.

Learning experience

Practical, critical, and collaborative.

Build a Digital Portfolio

Develop concrete examples and a final project aligned with your professional interests.

Evaluate Tools Critically

Assess AI tools and design meaningful, accessible learning experiences around them.

Design for Your Context

Create AI-enhanced learning resources for your own teaching environment.

Center Ethics and Equity

Support all learners through thoughtful, inclusive approaches to AI.

Scaffold Learning

Use generative AI to support learning without offloading the essential work students need to do.

Learn with Colleagues

Refine your ideas through feedback and collaboration in a diverse educational community.

Who should attend

Built for postsecondary education.

The course is designed for faculty and lecturers, instructional designers, faculty development staff, and other professionals who support higher education teaching.
